title: Politics explained
description: The government has approved higher Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for 14 Kharif crops for the 2026-27 season. MSP is a guaranteed price at which the government .

faq.a: Kharif crops are monsoon crops, sown at the beginning of the monsoon season (June-July) and harvested after the monsoon (September-October). Examples include paddy (rice), maize, jowar, bajra, tur, moong, cotton, and groundnut.

The MSP is calculated based on the cost of production (COP) of a crop, which includes expenses like seeds, fertilisers, hired labour, irrigation, and rent for leased land. The government aims to fix MSP at least 1.5 times the all-India weighted average cost of production.

faq.q: Does MSP help all farmers equally?
faq.a: The effectiveness of MSP varies. Farmers in states with robust procurement systems (like Punjab and Haryana for paddy and wheat) benefit more directly. Awareness of MSP and access to procurement centres can also be challenges for some farmers.

faq.q: What happens to the crops procured by the government at MSP?
faq.a: The crops procured at MSP are primarily used for the Public Distribution System (PDS), where essential food grains are distributed to eligible households at subsidised prices. They also help build buffer stocks to ensure food security during shortages.
